Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, Stereograph Cards, LOT 3531-2, LC-USZ62-61412, LC-DIG-stereo-1s42957 (item 2005694905).
author: E. W. Kelley

locator: The left-hand frame: a maid standing at the front door of a brick house, full length at about three metres, a uniformed postman with his mail bag on the step beside her.
rights_note: LOC rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on publication.' Used only as a reference picture the 1904 house maid is judged against and as the cut of her dress and apron (T-3448); nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-07 (T-3448) from the master TIFF; the catalogue gives the date as c1904 and marks its caption-card data 'unverified, old data', and the card's own handwritten line gives 1904. The maid wears a dark long-sleeved dress to the floor with tucks low on the skirt, a white turned-down collar at a high neck, a white bib apron whose broad scalloped and frilled straps stand out over the shoulders, the apron reaching nearly to the hem, and a small white frilled cap on full drawn-up hair. A staged comic scene, not Chicago and not of any named servant.
note: One of the 1904 house maid reference set's photographs (data/people_match/reference_sets/maid_1904.json).
what_it_supplies: a house maid's dark dress, white collar, bib apron with frilled straps and white cap, as worn at a front door in 1904
how long the apron is against the skirt, and how the straps sit over the shoulders
what_it_does_not_supply: colour (a monochrome print): black is the usual reading of the dress, not a measurement
anything about Chicago, the Glessner household or Mary Reynolds; no likeness is asserted
